correctness.rationale: Connectivity is partitioned into all subsets minus empty and within-one-part non-singleton subsets, producing a character-sum identity with no overlap. For \(N-t\) even all nontrivial coefficients are odd and hence nonzero; for \(N-t\) odd an explicit all-parts-nonzero frequency of weight (\(\(N+t\)-1\))/2 gives zero. Feasible all-parts-nonzero weights (\(N+t\))/2 or (\(N+t\)+1)/2 attain the sharp smallest modulus 1 or 2. A coefficient product counts every zero frequency exactly once. A union bound and Stirling prove the balanced-parameter asymptotic. Standalone integer FWHT and a distinct coefficient enumeration agree for 269 tuples through \(N=11\), but finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The domain is the canonical node-reliability family of all nonempty connected induced vertex sets. Its counting-convolution kernel asks whether translated counts determine a signal; this is an exact graph-associated Fourier invariant, not a free numerical slice. All multipartite profiles are classified, including the counterintuitive parity-sensitive invertibility criterion, the exact rank/nullity coefficient formula, sharp positive recovery condition numbers, and a quantitative asymptotic nullspace transition. Such full reconstruction data are absent from scalar connected-set counting. Its proof is short but its complete, natural parameter scope and stability interpretation provide substantive usefulness.
